transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Kim (BlueNova), Marcus Li (BlueNova), Priya Rao (BlueNova)

Summary (auto): Maya/Ethan did a hands-on SDK hotseat: auth flows, local sandbox boot, sample Python/TS snippets, plus quick Optimize tips. BlueNova to run a latency script and follow up on security.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i have Ethan with me the SE, we'll do a quick interactive hotseat where you throw us your environment questions and we'll walk the SDK quickstarts and auth flows.
00:18 Sofia: Hi Maya, thanks. We're mostly curious about how fast we can get a minimal auth rotation in CI and how to run things locally without risking keys.
00:30 Marcus: Also want to see batching settings — our inference cost is jumping on spikes.
00:45 Ethan: Great, we'll start with the Python quickstart then show TypeScript. I'll share a sandbox invite so keys are scoped to a dev env. Quick note: the sandbox keys expire, and we recommend rotating with your KMS as part of CI.
01:05 Priya: Can you show the console too? we want to see cost breakdowns per route.
01:12 Maya: Yep console demo after the quick SDK snippets. We'll also show Optimize UI where we surface suggested batching and cache settings.

03:40 Ethan: (screen share) Alright in the repo, there's a quickstart folder. Python file main.py — authenticate by setting REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-xxx. Then run python main.py — it calls the /v1/generate endpoint via the SDK.
04:05 Sofia: Does the SDK auto-retry on 429s or should we implement backoff?
04:12 Ethan: SDK has basic retry built-in but we recommend granular control in prod; we showed an example backoff wrapper in the utils/ folder. Not all 429s should be retried, sometimes it's capacity fallbacks.
05:00 Ethan: Switching to TypeScript — the TS client uses REDWOOD_API_KEY too or you can pass a credential provider; example code: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) and then client.generate(...).
05:35 Marcus: For local dev, are there secrets helpers? we use dotenv and GitHub Actions.
05:40 Ethan: Yes, we include a .env.example and a github actions snippet. For rotation use our recommended pattern: store encrypted key in your KMS, have a short-lived CI job that pulls decrypts and injects it into the job environment as REDWOOD_API_KEY. We also support workload identity for GCP.
06:22 Sofia: You mentioned role-based access — can we scope keys to models or routes?
06:30 Maya: Currently keys are scoped to accounts/teams; RBAC is in the console for routes and tokens. You can create tokens with limited scopes for embeddings-only or generate-only.
07:05 Priya: Walk us through the sandbox invite — how isolated is it?
07:10 Ethan: Sandbox is per-account with isolated keys and separate quota; no access to production logs. It's great for perf testing but not for PHI. For PHI you'd use Private with VPC + KMS.

09:00 Maya: Ok next Optimize basics. In the console Optimize tab we surface batching recommendations based on recent traffic and sequence length histogram. We'll demo toggling batching from conservative to aggressive and show cost/latency estimate.
09:28 Ethan: Live demo: setting batch window from 20ms to 80ms — latency rises slightly but cost per token drops. We'll also enable prefix caching for repeated prompts which can save a lot if you have many similar inputs.
10:05 Marcus: How does caching interact with KV cache for chat sessions?
10:12 Ethan: caching is prefix/KV aware; if you pin model version and use session keys, the runtime can reuse KV cache which reduces compute for multi-turn sessions. There's a tradeoff with memory.

12:30 Sofia: We want to run a baseline, what should we measure?
12:40 Ethan: Measure cold-start latency, P95 under steady QPS (5, 20, 100), token throughput, and tail latencies during bursts. We'll provide a script that hits the sandbox and emits token-level timings.
13:10 Maya: We'll attach the latency script to the ticket after the call.

15:00 (demo interruption) Marcus: sorry, quick sec — our infra team uses limited outbound egress; do you need special egress to talk to Redwood hosted endpoints?
15:10 Ethan: Only standard HTTPS outbound. For Private we can host in your VPC with no egress to public internet; the control plane still needs connectivity for management unless you choose fully air-gapped on-prem.
15:35 Sofia: On security, do you have SOC2 and audit logs?
15:40 Maya: Yes SOC 2 Type II, and audit logs are available in the console for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we provide redacted logs and can set retention policies. We'll send the security pack.

18:20 Ethan: Back to code: example batching config in client config: { batching: { enabled: true, maxBatchSize: 8, maxWaitMs: 50 } } — that's in our SDK docs. For aggressive throughput you'd want larger batch sizes and longer wait windows, but test for p95 tradeoffs.
19:05 Marcus: Any tips on quantization for cost savings?
19:10 Ethan: For on-prem or Dedicated you can enable INT8 quantization in the model profile; we recommend running evals as quality can drop on some models. Optimize has suggested quant profiles per model.
19:40 Priya: What about webhooks and function-calling? we want structured results.
19:46 Maya: SDK supports streaming and function-calling; we have examples for returning JSON schema validated responses using the function-calling helper. We'll share a small sample repo.

22:00 (rough transcript, some crosstalk) Sofia: Are there rate limits we should watch for?
22:08 Ethan: Sandbox has soft limits, Hosted prod has documented quotas per plan; Dedicated has reserved capacity so rate limits are at the GPU pool level. If you need bursts we can configure autoscale/burst options.

25:30 Maya: Let's do the hotseat: Marcus — send your screen and show your current local test script?
25:45 Marcus: Sure — (shares) this is a basic cURL that sends prompt text, we see p95 of 450ms on our side.
26:05 Ethan: Ok that's helpful; what's your average prompt length?
26:12 Marcus: about 120 tokens including system prompt.
26:20 Ethan: For those lengths, batching of 4-6 with maxWaitMs 40ms often gives a good sweet spot. Also consider prefix caching if many prompts share a similar system instruction.
27:00 Sofia: Our CI rotates keys monthly; any gotchas?
27:05 Maya: Ensure old tokens are revoked and that jobs handle token refresh failures gracefully; we provide a token revoke endpoint and advise exponential backoff on auth failures.

30:10 Priya: Can you show the console route-level cost breakdown?
30:20 Maya: (screen) Here — per-route token counts, model usage, and cost overlays. You can pin a route to a cheaper model variant and fallback to higher-cost model when latency spikes.
31:05 Marcus: How are rollouts handled? can we do canary?
31:12 Ethan: Yes you can configure route rollouts with percentages and automatic fallback rules based on error rate and latency. We also expose tracing hooks for SRE.

34:00 Sofia: A security question: Do you keep full input logs for Hosted?
34:10 Maya: By default hosted keeps request/response logs for 30 days and you can opt out or redact sensitive fields; Dedicated/Private customers can choose different retention and export raw logs to their S3/KMS-protected stores.
34:40 Marcus: Will we be able to push logs to our SIEM?
34:45 Maya: Yes via log export. We'll include the sample Lambda/forwarder in the repo.

37:20 Ethan: Quick note on SDK releases — we maintain semver, and breaking changes are rare; we publish migration guides in the changelog. Try pinning patch releases in prod.
37:40 Priya: If we want Private deployment, what's the timeline?
37:45 Maya: Typical Private onboarding is 6-10 weeks after contract — depends on your infra and compliance needs. We'll scope after security deep dive.

40:10 (wrap-up demo) Ethan: We'll drop the sample docker-compose that spins a local mock of the API for dev (auth stub + replay). That helps run unit tests without hitting hosted endpoints.
40:30 Sofia: That would be perfect, we prefer local mocks for dev.

44:00 Maya: Recap: we'll send sandbox invite + sample repos, attach the latency script, Security pack, and pricing brief. BlueNova to run baseline and we'll reconvene for security/pvt scoping.
44:30 Priya: Sounds good. Who's the main contact?
44:35 Sofia: I'll own the bench tests; Marcus will do infra testing; Priya will coordinate with product.
44:50 Maya: Great — I'll put the next steps into the ticket and sync calendars for the security deep dive.

51:00 (meeting close) Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email.
51:07 Sofia: Thanks all.

Notes: transcript has some auto-sub errors: Redwood product names sometimes transcribed as ‘Redwood run’ etc, and some technical terms slightly mangled.
